pros: Cartesian metric uniformity across Pune municipal extent
Standard 2D array representation directly consumable by CNNs and PyTorch tensors
Simple zonal statistics without area distortion
cons: Artificial square boundaries do not follow natural street corridors or wards
Fractional boundary intersection with municipal limits

candidate_2_uber_h3_resolution_9.unit_name: Uber H3 Discrete Global Grid System (Resolution 9)
pros: Uniform distance to all 6 adjacent neighbors (optimal for heat diffusion & contagion)
Standardized integer cell indexing (int64) for ultra-fast database joins
Global scalability and direct mapping to mobility/demographic datasets
cons: Non-hierarchical aperture-7 area nesting across resolutions
Requires geodesic zonal aggregation rather than planar array slicing
candidate_2_uber_h3_resolution_9.suitability_score: HIGH (for spatial connectivity and intervention modeling)

candidate_3_uber_h3_resolution_8.unit_name: Uber H3 Discrete Global Grid System (Resolution 8)
candidate_3_uber_h3_resolution_8.suitability_score: MEDIUM (good for macro-neighborhood analysis, too coarse for block-level cool roofs)

pros: Direct alignment with civic budgetary and municipal implementation mechanisms
cons: High variance in ward area (Modifiable Areal Unit Problem - MAUP)
candidate_4_administrative_wards.suitability_score: REPORTING_ONLY (downstream aggregation target, not primary modeling mesh)

deferred_decision_statement: The final analytical spatial unit (e.g., 250m planar metric grid vs. H3 resolution 9) is intentionally deferred to Phase 1B. All Phase 1A.8 products are strictly stored at their native resolutions to enable lossless, mathematically rigorous aggregation to whichever target geometry is formally ratified.
